functions.name: WithKeyFile
functions.description: Sets up a keyfile for internal authentication between members of a MongoDB replica set, with the specified `keyValue` as the content of the file.
functions.remarks:
The keyfile is a shared secret. Every member of the replica set (or sharded cluster) should have the same keyfile, and possession of that secret is what authenticates a connection as "a legitimate member of this cluster."
See https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/deploy-replica-set-with-keyfile-access-control/

parameters.name: keyValue
parameters.description: The content of the keyfile. This is a shared secret: every member of the replica set has to be given the same value, and anything holding it can authenticate as a member of the cluster.

fields.name: KeyFilePath
fields.description: The absolute path the keyfile is mounted at inside the container, which has to include a file name. Defaults to `/etc/rs.key`.

functions.name: WithMember
functions.description: Adds a MongoDB server resource as a member of the replica set.
functions.remarks:
Internally calls the following methods on the member's builder:
- Configures the member's replica set name and command-line arguments without initializing a separate single-member set. Do not call `WithReplicaSet` on these members.
- `WithKeyFile` to set the key file parameter on the member resource, which is required for internal authentication between replica set members.
- `WithTlsAllowInvalidCertificates` because members authenticate to each other with the same certificate they serve to clients, which does not carry a `clientAuth` extended key usage.
- `WithHttpsDeveloperCertificate``1`, unless the member already has certificate configuration of its own. TLS is required for members of a replica set, because the split-horizon member hostname advertisement performed by the server operates on top of SNI.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: The MongoDB server resource that represents the member to add to this replica set.

functions.name: WithRepl
functions.description: Adds a REPL command that opens an authenticated MongoDB shell in the dashboard terminal dock.
functions.remarks:
This command is opt-in and available only in run mode. Dashboard users who can execute resource commands
can run commands with the resource's configured credentials. Enable it only for trusted dashboard users,
especially when sharing the dashboard through a tunnel or remote development environment.

functions.name: WithReplicaSet
functions.description: Configures and initializes the MongoDB server as a single-member replica set for local development.
functions.remarks:
Enables transactions and change streams without changing database resources or references. The server becomes
healthy only after initialization and primary election. Connections use the server's normal endpoint directly;
a developer certificate, topology discovery, and fixed host ports are not required.
A key file is generated for authentication unless `WithKeyFile` was called first.
Existing single-member data is reused without reconfiguration. Keep the set name and credentials unchanged when
reusing a data volume. Publishing and deploying this configuration are not supported.
Unlike the previous low-level behavior of this experimental method, this method initializes the set.
For multiple members, use `AddMongoDBReplicaSet` and
`WithMember` instead, without calling this method on the members.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The replica set name. Defaults to the resource name, or the name previously configured by this method.

functions.name: WithTlsAllowInvalidCertificates
functions.description: Configures the MongoDB server to accept TLS connections whose peer certificate cannot be validated, by passing `--tlsAllowInvalidCertificates` to `mongod`.
functions.remarks:
This weakens certificate authentication and should only be used when a peer legitimately cannot present a
certificate this server is able to validate. It is what
`WithMember`
uses today, because replica set members authenticate to each other with the same certificate they serve to clients
and that certificate does not carry a `clientAuth` extended key usage.
See https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod/#std-option-mongod.--tlsAllowInvalidCertificates
```
var mongo = builder.AddMongoDB("mongo")
.WithTlsAllowInvalidCertificates();
```

functions.name: WithTlsMode
functions.description: Configures the `--tlsMode` the MongoDB server is started with when TLS is active.
functions.remarks:
TLS itself is not turned on by this method. A MongoDB server resource serves TLS whenever an HTTPS/TLS certificate
is available for it — by default the ASP.NET Core developer certificate — and serves plain TCP otherwise. Use
`WithHttpsDeveloperCertificate``1` or
`WithHttpsCertificate``1` to opt in explicitly, and
`WithoutHttpsCertificate``1` to opt out. This method only controls
how strict the server is about TLS on incoming connections once TLS is active; the default is
`RequireTls`.
See https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options/#mongodb-setting-net.tls.mode
Let clients connect either with or without TLS:
```
var mongo = builder.AddMongoDB("mongo")
.WithTlsMode(MongoDBTlsMode.PreferTls);
```

fields.name: Mode
fields.description: The TLS mode to run the MongoDB server in.

enumTypes.name: MongoDBTlsMode
enumTypes.description: Defines the TLS mode for MongoDB server.

members.name: MongoDBTlsModeAllowTls
members.description: Connections between servers do not use TLS. For incoming connections, the server accepts both TLS and non-TLS.

members.name: MongoDBTlsModePreferTls
members.description: Connections between servers use TLS. For incoming connections, the server accepts both TLS and non-TLS.

members.name: MongoDBTlsModeRequireTls
members.description: The server uses and accepts only TLS encrypted connections.
